decisions.reason: The source expands label coverage and specifies label design, but it does not change the Danish language or placeholder-text requirements.
Adding matching labels to every interactive field does not change the requirement to preserve Title-field formatting during interaction.
The label coverage and design decision does not necessarily alter the field implementation architecture or editable-text mechanism.
The source does not change how placeholder text clears or how fields behave when activated.
The new label design requirement does not resolve or change the separate unresolved requirement for grey editable-field cues.
Requiring labels for interactive fields does not change the date field's calendar-dropdown entry method.
The source does not modify the checklist-and-dropdown control configuration.
Interactive-field label coverage and design are unrelated to tab-driven list hierarchy behavior.
The source specifies a field-label requirement but does not change the catalog-wide style-system coverage or source style system.
The control-label design reference does not affect graphic bullet appearance, alignment, scaling, or color.
Interactive control labels are distinct from image and table caption labels, so the caption typography and style name remain unchanged.
Although earlier evidence mentioned interactive-field labels alongside theme colors, the source decision does not change the required theme-color palette.
